cards.title: E2E suites run the shell's own trust snapshot, not hand-wired NOTHING_GATED deps
acceptance: first sight: a ledgerbox tab with NO origins row, wired through shell.ts (snapshot = snapshotOf over the seeded table/tabs/tools), auto-turn.ndjson, send('what is overdue?') -> the first /run body carries gated_origins == ['host:ledgerbox'], page.calls == [], exactly one card with action host.ledgerbox.list_overdue

registered and accepted: the same tab with an enabled origins row whose contracts are contractOf(each PAGE_TOOL), auto-turn.ndjson -> /run body gated_origins == [] and gated_tools == [], page.names() == ['list_overdue'], no card (the existing AUTO claim, now reached through the deciding input)
pinned: enabled row with overrides {list_overdue: 'GATED'}, auto-turn.ndjson -> /run body gated_tools == ['host.ledgerbox.list_overdue'], page untouched, one card for list_overdue

contract drift (ADR 0100): enabled row whose accepted contract for list_overdue says reversible:true/internal while the page now publishes reversible:false/external -> gated_tools contains host.ledgerbox.list_overdue, page untouched, one card

switched off: origins row enabled:false, auto-turn.ndjson -> /run body disabled_origins == ['host:ledgerbox'], the stream's tool.result for list_overdue is refused with foreign_origin, page.calls == []

apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:887 - snapshotFrom falls back to NOTHING_GATED when a surface wires no gated reader, so every ledgerbox e2e turn tells the daemon nothing is gated

cards.body:
## Summary
Every ledgerbox end-to-end suite certifies a panel configuration the shipped shell can never be in: its deps are hand-wired with no trust table, so `snapshotFrom` sends `NOTHING_GATED` and the daemon is told no app is first-sight, pinned, drifted or switched off. Introduce one `e2e/support/shell.ts` that builds RunDeps/VoiceDeps from a seeded origins table, tab list and tool list through the shell's own `snapshotOf`, migrate the four hand-wirings onto it, and add the ADR 0063/0100 trust cases end to end.

## Description
The AUTO-turn claim in run.e2e (`page.names() == ['list_overdue']`, no card) is true only because the deciding input is absent: with the shipped `LIVE.snapshot`, a ledgerbox tab nobody registered goes out as `gated_origins: ['host:ledgerbox']` and the harness's `_tightened` turns the AUTO call into a card. That is test-harness/unreached-decisions-pin-nothing: the suite asserts a value a default would produce too. The trust composition (gatedListsOf, contractDriftsOf, disabledOriginsOf, all folded into snapshotOf) is unit-tested in the store and the daemon's gate is unit-tested in Python, but the hop that joins them, the /run body the panel really sends and the card the real daemon really files from it, has no case. shell.ts takes `{ origins: rows, contracts, tabs, tools, call }` and returns deps whose `snapshot` is `snapshotOf(...)`, exactly the LIVE shape minus Tauri; shadowrunr's `registeredTable`/`gatedFor` become its first caller.

## Flow
- shell.ts: `shellDeps({ daemon, table, tab, tools, call, fetchImpl })` -> RunDeps with snapshot/gated/disabledOrigins/tab, and `voiceShellDeps(...)` the same for VoiceDeps; helpers `firstSight()`, `registered(tools, overrides?)`, `switchedOff()` build the TrustTable.
- run.e2e and voice.e2e live() call it with `registered(PAGE_TOOLS)`, so every existing claim still holds and now holds for the reason the product gives.
- trust.e2e.test.ts adds first sight, pin, drift and switched-off over auto-turn.ndjson, plus the spoken first-sight case.
- loop.ts's registeredTable/gatedFor move into shell.ts; wireLoop calls it.

## Expected impact
A regression in any of the four trust rules on the shell side (a reader dropped from snapshotOf, a renamed body field, a slug/origin mix-up in catalogIdOf) turns an e2e case red instead of shipping a panel that tells the gate nothing. Four hand-wired deps become one, so the next RunDeps field a surface must wire is wired once.

## Evaluation
Claim: the e2e suites reach the trust decision the shipped shell makes and certify it over the real wire.
Before: 0 of 5 trust cases (1-5) exist; the AUTO claim passes through NOTHING_GATED
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

NOTHING_GATED`. stores/run.ts:566 `snapshot: () => snapshotOf(useOrigins.getState(), useTabs.getState().tabs, useTools.getState().byTab, useTabs.getState().recent)`. hooks.py:456-462 `return (str(origin) in ctx.gated_origins or entry.name in ctx.gated_tools or _tainted(entry, ctx) or another_tab(entry, ctx))`. grep 'gated\|snapshot' apps/desktop/e2e/*.ts -> only comments and transcript names; the only e2e caller of gatedListsOf is shadowrunr/support/loop.ts:146.

cards.title: Pilot report answers 'better or worse than last run': per-case deltas and a verdict
acceptance: comparePilot(prev, curr) with the same case ids where curr's 'shape-malakor' has calls_before_content 4 -> 1 and ok stays true -> that case row is 'better' with delta -3 and the run verdict is 'better'
a case that was ok:true and is now ok:false -> row 'regressed' naming the new failure strings, and the run verdict is 'worse' whatever the other rows say
a case whose unknown_tools gains a name it did not have -> 'regressed' with the new name listed, even when its calls_before_content improved

outcome-conditioned cost (eval-harness/outcome-conditioned-cost): cost and turn deltas are computed only over cases ok in BOTH runs; a case that failed in either run is reported with its cost but excluded from the cost delta, and the summary states 'cost over N of M cases'
case sets differ: a case only in curr is 'new', only in prev is 'gone'; neither enters any delta and the verdict line names them
no previous run (prev = null) -> pilotMarkdown output is byte-identical to today's (no comparison section)

previousReport(outRoot, currentStamp) picks the newest out/<stamp>/report.json older than currentStamp and skips a stamp folder whose report.json is missing or unparseable, returning null when none qualifies

pilotMarkdown(title, reports, comparison) renders a 'Since <prev stamp>' table (case, verdict, before-content delta, turns delta, cards delta, cost delta) above today's summary table, and the first line under the title is the one-word verdict
premise: apps/desktop/e2e/shadowrunr/shadowrunr.live.e2e.test.ts:76 - every live run writes out/<stamp>/report.json and report.md into a fresh folder; nothing ever reads a previous one
apps/desktop/e2e/support/pilot.ts:85 - pilotMarkdown renders one run in isolation: per-case turns, calls, before-content, unknown tool, cards, cost, wall time, with no baseline column

apps/desktop/e2e/support/pilot.ts:2 - the pilot's stated question is 'does she orient smoothly and spend her turns on content', which is a comparative question (did this exposure change make orientation better) the report cannot answer
apps/desktop/e2e/support/pilot.ts:64 - orientationOf already computes the per-case measure a comparison needs (calls_before_content, unknown_tools)
apps/desktop/e2e/shadowrunr/.gitignore - out/ is local and accumulates one folder per run, so the baseline is already on disk
cards.rollback: Two commits (pure comparePilot/previousReport + markdown section with their tests; the live test wiring the previous report in); reverting the second leaves an unused, tested function, reverting both restores today's report exactly (case 6 pins that).

cards.body:
## Summary
The live pilot (`/open verify` level 2) is how an operator learns whether a change to an app's exposure (its orient tools, its descriptions, its catalogue) made Athena orient faster and spend her turns on content. Each run writes a careful report, but only of itself; the operator has to open two markdown files and diff a table by eye to answer the one question the pilot exists for. Add a comparison mode: the live test loads the newest earlier report.json, `comparePilot` produces per-case verdicts and deltas, and the report opens with one word: better, worse or same.

## Description
The data is already there: report.json carries every CaseReport, and out/ keeps every run. What is missing is the rule for comparing two runs honestly. The rule follows the registry's eval-harness techniques: a regression in ok or a newly named unknown tool outranks any efficiency gain (failure-signatures-beside-the-pass-rate); cost and turn deltas are taken only over cases that reached an answer in both runs (outcome-conditioned-cost); case sets that differ are named, never averaged over. The comparison is a pure function over two CaseReport arrays, so it is tested hermetically; the live test only finds the baseline and passes it in. With no baseline the report is exactly today's.

## Flow
- pilot.ts: `previousReport(outRoot, stamp)`, `comparePilot(prev, curr) -> { verdict, rows, costOver: {n, m}, added, gone }`, and `pilotMarkdown(title, reports, comparison?)`.
- shadowrunr.live.e2e.test.ts: flush() computes the comparison once against the baseline found in beforeAll and writes it into report.md and report.json (`comparison` key).
- pilot.e2e.test.ts: the eight cases over fixture CaseReports, no daemon, no browser.

## Expected impact
An operator re-running the pilot after changing an app's orient tools reads one line to know whether it helped, sees which case regressed and why, and is not misled by a cheaper run that got cheaper by failing. Any later app's pilot inherits it, since pilot.ts is app-agnostic.

## Evaluation
Claim: a pilot run states its verdict against the previous run, by rules that cannot reward failing cheaply.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no comparison exists)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
